title: Half-Life and the Numeric Age of Rocks
learningObjectives: Explain that half-life is the time for exactly one-half of parent atoms to decay to daughter atoms.
Use counts of remaining parent atoms and new daughter atoms to compute the numeric age of a rock in years.
Pair isotopically dated rocks with fossil-bearing rocks to assign numeric ages to the geologic time scale.

evidence.quote: The half-life of a radioactive isotope is the length of time required for exactly one-half of the parent atoms to decay to daughter atoms.
Each radioactive isotope has its own unique half-life.

explanations.text: A half-life is the time for exactly half of the radioactive parent atoms to decay to daughter atoms, and each isotope has its own unique half-life.

evidence.quote: A radioactive isotope (the parent) of one chemical element naturally converts to a stable isotope (the daughter)
The change from parent to daughter happens at a constant rate, called the half-life.

explanations.text: A radioactive parent isotope naturally converts to a stable daughter isotope at a constant rate called the half-life.

explanations.text: Minerals with natural radioactive elements are used to calculate a rock numeric age in years, and an isotopically dated rock is paired with fossil-bearing rocks to assign ages to the time scale.
